title: Types of sacrifice

D0.outcome: Names the main reasons for a sacrifice (open lines for an attack, deflect or decoy, break a blockade, win time, gain a lasting positional edge) and says each needs a stated payoff.

D1.outcome: Given a sacrifice, names its type and the payoff that justifies it.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, decides to accept or decline a sacrifice, and labels the verdict sound or practical.

D3.outcome: Calculates the declined lines and verifies the claim at the wins-or-mates level.

misconceptions: A sacrifice that wins in the book wins here.
A sacrificed pawn is a lost pawn (or: tempo is always worth more than a pawn).
sources: docs/curriculum-map-v1.md §2 S6 (Spielmann, Tal, [R] in the map)
conditions: Calculate before sacrificing; the compensation must survive the first accurate reply.
Sacrifices are labelled 'practical, not sound' where unverified.
contrasts: A famous sacrifice whose declined line refutes it.
A positional sacrifice for a blockade presented as sound without checking.
A sacrifice that wins the same material by simpler means.

soft_prereq_notes.TAC.DECOY.D1: decoy and deflection are the commonest sacrifice types
